newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TELCO dips 6 pct on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: India's TELCO dips 6 pct on fund sales.

text.p: Shares of Indian truckmaker TELCO dipped 23.50 rupees or 6.26 percent to 352 rupees on the Bombay bourse on Friday as foreign funds turned sellers, traders said.
Auto analysts said rumours that TELCO's October sales were likely to show a sharp slowdown from the year-ago were untrue.

"Total sales for October are at 16,822 vehicles, up 26.2 percent from the year-ago and down 5.2 percent from September which is traditionally when sales peak," said an auto analyst at a foreign brokerage firm, quoting unofficial figures.
Official auto figures for October are due early next week.
Traders said a couple of funds were sellers and punters had jumped on the bandwagon hammering the stock price lower.
"Fundamentally, nothing has changed. But sentiment has taken a beating with many investors not expecting the stock to outperform in the next eight to ten months," the analyst said.
Fears of a slowdown in the economy -- confirmed by latest government data released on Wednesday -- have made some investors wary of truckmakers like TELCO and Ashok Leyland.
India's April-September industrial growth has slowed to 4.8 percent from 12.8 percent during the corresponding period last year.
